title: Reduce model-load tail latency with staged activation and verifier
creator: Marcus Li
description: Background: Large model cold-starts and checkpoint activations produce long and variable model-load latencies (high tail). Current loader activates entire weight sets and performs format validation synchronously which spikes 99th-percentile latencies and blocks routing decisions. Goal: introduce a staged weight activation protocol plus a lightweight verifier service (activation conductor) to reduce tail latency while preserving correctness and backward compatibility. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, rollout, and compatibility shims for older weight manifests.
acceptance_criteria: 99th-percentile model-load latency for 30B+ models reduced by >= 50% in our internal bench compared to current master
Loader supports a two-phase activation: header/manifest verification + prioritized shard activation + background finalization
No change to client API or model catalog entries; old manifests fall back to legacy synchronous activation when feature flag disabled
Activation conductor exposes metrics: staged_activation_time, verifier_success_rate, activated_shard_count, stalled_shards
End-to-end integration tests added: checkpoint-failure, partial-shard-network-failure, format-fallback
Feature gated behind runtime feature-flag with deterministic canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and automatic rollback on regression
implementation_notes: Introduce 'activation_conductor' actor in loader runtime responsible for sequencing shard activation based on priority and checksum verification
Phase 1 (header): stream and parse checkpoint manifest, run quick checksum of header sections, validate manifest schema and compatibility
Phase 2 (priority activation): identify shards required for initial inference (embedding/head KV, first N token layers) and activate them first; activate remaining shards in background
Phase 3 (finalization): run full sha256 checksums and optional lazy decompression/quantization-on-activate to finish activation
Add a lightweight verifier binary (Rust) that validates shard headers and produces a signed activation token to avoid re-checking across restarts
Introduce manifest version marker v2-alpha and negotiation: loader accepts v1 (legacy) and v2 (staged), with transparent fallback; catalog rewrite optional
Update checkpoint ingestion path to emit activation plan and metrics to the console telemetry topic
Bench harness: extend loadbench to simulate network latency and partial bandwidth conditions; measure p50/p95/p99 for cold start with and without staged activation
Upgrade dependency: bump protobuf 3.20 -> 3.26 to fix streaming parsing bug in manifest ingest (ensure compatibility with on-disk manifest schema)
Performance optimization: reuse mmap for inactive shards to reduce memory churn while background activation continues
migration_plan: Add support for manifest v2-alpha in loader while continuing to accept v1; write migration tool to annotate existing catalog manifests with 'staged_capable: false' when unknown
Run catalog scanner job (non-blocking) that marks popular models as staged-capable after verification
Communicate with ops: schedule a low-traffic canary window to enable feature-flag for Dedicated clusters
Provide runtime flags to force legacy behavior for any customer experiencing regressions
Document changes in internal Confluence doc and add a migration checklist for partners using on-prem packages
metrics_and_targets: Metric: staged_activation_latency_ms (target: p95 < 1s for initial shard set)
Metric: background_activation_traffic_bytes (monitor increase to avoid IO storms)
Dashboard: new 'Activation Conductor' panel in Console release runtime-2026.03 showing per-model activation traces
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Background activation causes I/O storms on shared hosts. Mitigation: rate-limit background activation and add token-bucket per-host throttling
Risk: Manifest parsing difference causes false negatives. Mitigation: keep full v1 compatibility and add exhaustive parser fuzz tests
Risk: Dependency bump (protobuf) introduces build or runtime incompatibilities. Mitigation: build-matrix CI and shadow-deploy to staging with legacy fallback enabled
Risk: Canaries detect user-visible regressions. Mitigation: force automatic rollback and circuit-breaker that reverts to legacy activation per-model
comments: 2026-02-10 Marcus Li: Triage notes - CPU and IO profiling on master shows large variance when activating > 100 shards concurrently. Proposal: staged activation with priority for head/KV layers. Adding Aisha to lead implementation.

2026-02-15 Aisha Kapoor: Design review - Shared draft posted to Confluence. Main open question: how to derive initial shard priority deterministically across model formats. Suggest using a 'priority_hint' in manifest header plus a fallback heuristic based on layer naming conventions.
2026-02-18 Marcus Li: Review feedback - please add compatibility tests for legacy manifests produced by historical exporter (pre-2024). Also add a stress test with slow network simulation.

2026-02-22 Aisha Kapoor: Implementation update - PoC conductor implemented; initial benchmark shows p99 drop from 11.8s -> 4.2s on loadbench for a 34B model with 120 shards. Still seeing IO spikes; introducing per-host rate-limit in next patch. Linked PR created: runtime/pull/7256
2026-02-25 Code Review (Taylor Chen): Requested changes - extract verifier to separate crate, add more unit tests for manifest edge cases, and log-level adjustments for noisy failures

2026-02-27 QA (Elena Ruiz): Integration tests - uncovered a race where background activation occasionally beats the verifier and causes duplicate writes; impact low but reproducible. Patch queued to introduce activation token handshake to idempotently skip already-activated shards.

2026-03-01 Aisha Kapoor: Ready for canary - feature flag added and console metrics wired. Planning phased rollout starting 2026-03-03 to 5% of Dedicated clusters. Will monitor model_load.p99_ms and verifier_failure_rate closely.
